web.title: Lord Hewell
web.description:
| Occupation | [Noble](/wiki/Nobles_of_Gilneas) |

**Lord Hewell** is a nobleman of [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_peninsula) who can be found at [Tempest's Reach](/wiki/Tempest%27s_Reach) during the [worgen starting experience](/wiki/Worgen_starting_experience). Though the eastern lords ([Lord Walden](/wiki/Lord_Walden) and [Baron Ashbury](/wiki/Baron_Ashbury)) took part in [Lord Godfrey](/wiki/Lord_Godfrey)'s plan to take [King Genn Greymane](/wiki/King_Genn_Greymane) captive in order to bargain with the [Forsaken](/wiki/Forsaken), Hewell refused to betray his king. Instead he remained by Greymane's side until [Krennan Aranas](/wiki/Krennan_Aranas) sent an [adventurer](/wiki/Adventurer) to help.

web.title: Lord Vincent Godfrey
web.description: **Lord Vincent Godfrey**[3] is a renegade nobleman from [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_peninsula) who opposed his king, [Genn Greymane](/wiki/Genn_Greymane), after discovering that Genn and many of his people had been afflicted with the [worgen](/wiki/Worgen) curse. After committing suicide rather than acknowledge a worgen as his lord, Godfrey's body was recovered and reanimated by the [Forsaken](/wiki/Forsaken), but after turning on them as well, he fled into the abandoned ruins of [Shadowfang Keep](/wiki/Shadowfang_Keep), where he and his followers remain.

web.title: Baron Ashbury
web.description: **Baron Ashbury** was an eastern nobleman from [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_(kingdom)).

web.title: Darius Crowley
web.description:
**Lord Darius Crowley** was once a [Gilnean](/wiki/Gilneas_(kingdom)) nobleman. A pro-[Alliance](/wiki/Alliance_of_Lordaeron) figure, he dissented with King [Genn Greymane](/wiki/Genn_Greymane)'s decision to separate his people with the [Greymane Wall](/wiki/Greymane_Wall). Crowley led the [Northgate Rebellion](/wiki/Northgate_Rebellion) that caused a civil war in [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_peninsula), during which he was imprisoned. When Gilneas was attacked by [worgen](/wiki/Worgen), he was freed and became a worgen himself.

At the time of the [Second War](/wiki/Second_War), Lord Crowley was a nobleman whose lands and people were in northern [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_(kingdom)), including some land outside of the border that would later be known as the [Greymane Wall](/wiki/Greymane_Wall). He owned the towns of [Pyrewood Village](/wiki/Pyrewood_Village) and [Ambermill](/wiki/Ambermill).

web.description:

web.title: Lord Hiram Creed
web.description:
**Lord Hiram Creed** was a [black](/wiki/Black_dragonflight)[drakonid](/wiki/Drakonid) who disguises themselves as an affluent [Gilnean](/wiki/Gilneas_(kingdom)) noble. Creed manipulated a group of Gilnean humans and worgen named the [Blackhowl](/wiki/Blackhowl) who occupied [Gilneas City](/wiki/Gilneas_City), and secretly infected them with his own draconic blood, which made them stronger but also unwittingly slowly turned them into his unwilling servants.

Given that Creed holds enough prestige to lead a force into Gilneas City without question and his affluency was not questioned by his followers, he was likely masquerading as a nobleman for a long time to build up that trust, or he has impersonated an actual nobleman.

web.title: Northgate Rebellion
web.description:
The **Northgate Rebellion**[1] (also spelled the **Northgate rebellion**)[2] was a civil war which occurred in the [Kingdom of Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_(kingdom)) between forces loyal to the Gilnean monarchy, and those who supported disillusioned nobleman [Darius Crowley](/wiki/Darius_Crowley), around the time of the end of the [Third War](/wiki/Third_War). It was named for the region in the north of [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_peninsula) around the [Greymane Wall](/wiki/Greymane_Wall).

Upon studying a map of Gilneas, the King's decision to close Gilneas's borders and construct the great wall would cut through the lands of a newer, but still well-respected nobleman by the name of [Lord Darius Crowley](/wiki/Lord_Darius_Crowley), as the noble's lands had the mountains as a natural barrier the wall could be built into.

Unable to remain idle as his king went about what Crowley considered to be "tyranny", the nobleman sent a platoon of his own soldiers, in the form of the [Gilneas Brigade](/wiki/Gilneas_Brigade_(Warcraft_III)), to aid the Alliance, as well as [Lady Jaina Proudmoore](/wiki/Lady_Jaina_Proudmoore)'s expedition to [Kalimdor](/wiki/Kalimdor).

web.title: Gilneas City
web.description: It was later revealed that [Lord Hiram Creed](/wiki/Lord_Hiram_Creed), leader of the [Blackhowl](/wiki/Blackhowl), rules over most of the Gilneans in the area. In reality, Creed was a [black dragon](/wiki/Black_dragon) disguised as a Gilnean nobleman. He and his Blackhowl servants occupied much of Gilneas City, having taken out several Forsaken assassination attempts on him. He had apparently used his own draconic blood to further the Blackhowl's obedience and skills.

web.title: Nobles of Gilneas
web.description:
The **nobles of Gilneas** are the ruling class of the [kingdom of Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_(kingdom)). Some were slain during the [civil war](/wiki/Northgate_Rebellion), while others were turned into [worgen](/wiki/Worgen) or [Forsaken](/wiki/Forsaken) during the [Forsaken invasion](/wiki/Invasion_of_Gilneas). Others remain [human](/wiki/Human) in exile from their homeland.[1]

[Baron Longshore](/wiki/Baron_Longshore) states that he was once a legitimate baron of Gilneas; though where his lands would have been, or if someone else was given jurisdiction over them, is unknown.

web.title: Commander Springvale
web.description: Commander Springvale Commander Springvale is the third boss in Shadowfang Keep. By dungeon teleport, he is located in the Keep's chapel. Springvale was a paladin and the commander at the head of Baron Silverlaine's troops. He was killed with the other inhabitants of the keep by worgen, summoned by Archmage Arugal from the Emerald Dream to aid Gilneans against the Scourge.[2] Since then, his ghost haunts the keep, using unholy strikes to avenge his lord.

web.title: Havenswood
web.description: Havenswood is an Island Expedition location, home to an abandoned Gilnean settlement and castle.[1] It is inhabited by feral worgen, Old God minions, and dark necromancers.[2] Any method of reaching the upper town appears to have been removed. Whatever remains of the inhabitants in the lower areas of the island have been transformed into worgen; led by several druid worgen women. The males appear to almost all be feral,[3] while the women seem to have some semblance of control.[4][5] ... - Havenswood is named similarly to Pyrewood, another Gilnean settlement. - Something terrible happened here, which resulted in the raising of an undead horse.[7] [Lord Woofington] was given his title after the rest of the denizens of the island succumbed to madness. ... Due to being overwhelmed by feral worgen and being a Gilnean settlement, Havenswood's island is probably located close to Gilneas and/or Silverpine Forest.

web.title: Jarod Shadowsong
web.description: Jarod is first seen in Bradensbrook, a town of human refugees who escaped from the Gilnean lands years ago during the Scourge uprising. The nearby Black Rook Hold has become plagued by undead night elves, and Jarod has come to investigate while also searching for his sister, but the Gilneans do not trust him. After having an adventurer prove his trustworthiness, Jarod ventured to Black Rook Hold and found that Lord Kur'talos Ravencrest's body had gone missing, raised along with the other undead in the fortress. Jarod and the adventurer put the night elf spirits to rest while also searching for his captured sister. ... - Refugee Leadership

web.title: Duskhaven
web.description: Duskhaven was a town located along the southwestern coast of Gilneas. Gwen Armstead was its mayor. It was the location that the evacuees from Gilneas City fled to as the worgen overran the capital. One day before the attack on Gilneas City, the town witnessed a murder by the Starlight Slasher. With the earthquakes caused by the Cataclysm, the land beneath Duskhaven crumbled, and the town was swallowed by the sea. Its underwater ruins can be visited on the Gilnean coast. ## NPCs Guards - Duskhaven Watchman Merchants ... Quest givers - Prince Liam Greymane(outskirts only) - Slain Watchman(outskirts) - Gwen Armstead - Krennan Aranas - Lord Godfrey ... As Gwen Armstead was the major of Grimmburg,[2] and with the description of [3] Incomplete Cartography implying the town's fate, it is very likely that Duskhaven was initially concepted as Grimmburg. Warden Blackwell, Krennan Aranas, Huntsman Russell, Gilnean Bloodhounds, Grimmburg Militias, Grimmburg Watchmen, Orc Scouts, and Krugg Worgmaw were present here. Lieutenant Wright was out of the town, on the "frontlines".

web.title: Kul Tiras - Wowpedia - Your wiki guide to the World of Warcraft
web.description: Kul Tiras (also spelled Kul'Tiras;[1][2] pronounced KOOL-teer-AHS)[3] is an archipelago located in the Great Sea, west of the Eastern Kingdoms. The islands are home to the human nation of the same name, having originally been discovered and colonized by Gilnean sailors from the mainland Eastern Kingdoms.[4] Kul Tiras has played host to a mighty maritime tradition since it was first settled by humans. During the Second War, it was the largest naval force in Azeroth and a major contributor to the war effort against the Orcish Horde. Since then, and with the eventual disintegration of the Alliance of Lordaeron, Kul Tiras became significantly more isolated and less involved on the world stage. ... 2,700 years BDP, after the Troll Wars, the humans of Arathor traveled to various regions. Some human sailors left Gilneas and found a large island full of metal ores and other resources. Following their arrival in Kul Tiras, the human colonists were attacked by the native Drust. The war that ensued led the large and hardy race, who lived in Drustvar, to extinction.[7] ... Sometime after the third invasion of the Burning Legion, the Alliance came to the island seeking the powerful navy of Kul Tiras to aid in their new war against the Horde. The Alliance untangled a web of betrayal and dark magic as they encountered power-hungry pirates, witches wielding death magic, mystical tidesages, and more. Lady Jaina Proudmoore became Lord Admiral of Kul Tiras and the nation rejoined the Alliance. Kul Tiras took part in the faction war with the Horde, including rooting out Horde outposts on its territory and fighting off Horde Faction Assaults.

The harvest-witches would use their primitive druidic skills to cultivate crops, but almost "died out" as Gilneas developed, though, when the nation fell into famine, it was the druids who, as Celestine claims, "called upon the earth's blessing and restored the harvest". [13] When Kul Tiras was founded by Gilnean sailors, it is possible that some harvest-witches brought some of their teachings, but modern Kul Tiran druids claim only the Thornspeakers of the Drust vrykul Ulfar as the source of their druidry, who says some of his people became part of human society and their descendants hear the "call of the wild". - — Flavor text
**Countess Ashmore** is a [blue dragon](/wiki/Blue_dragon)[1] featured in the *[The Witchwood](/wiki/Hearthstone:_The_Witchwood)* expansion for *[Hearthstone](/wiki/Hearthstone_(game))*.
The countess is an enigma, and no one in [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_peninsula) seems to have heard of her noble line prior to the Witchwood curse, but suddenly, the records show an Ashmore family tree stretching all the way back to pre-[Alliance](/wiki/Alliance_of_Lordaeron) days, written in a hand none of the royal scribes recognize. She's taken up residence in an old manor that's been abandoned since before the first battle of Gilneas, but while some claim that many voices can be heard emerging from the old estate, she's the only one who's been seen entering or leaving. It's rumored that Ashmore is researching the curse, and she has been asking questions of those who claim to have witnessed dragons in the wood. It is not clear if Ashmore is truly the scion of a forgotten noble family returned home in a time of need, or if she is something much more dangerous.[2]

web.title: Gilneas (kingdom)
web.description: The **kingdom of Gilneas**[1] (pronounced "Gil-NEIGH-uhs"), or the **Gilnean kingdom**,[2] is one of the [seven human](/wiki/Seven_Kingdoms) [kingdoms](/wiki/Kingdom) and is located in the [peninsula of Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_peninsula), situated southwest of [Silverpine Forest](/wiki/Silverpine_Forest) on the continent of [Lordaeron](/wiki/Lordaeron). It is ruled by King [Genn Greymane](/wiki/Genn_Greymane) of the [Greymane family](/wiki/Greymane_family).

web.title: Ruins of Gilneas
web.description:
The **Ruins of Gilneas** is a peninsula southwest of [Silverpine Forest](/wiki/Silverpine_Forest) on the continent of [Lordaeron](/wiki/Lordaeron). It is the name for the [Gilneas zone](/wiki/Gilneas_(starting_zone)) after the events of the [worgen starting experience](/wiki/Worgen_starting_experience).

Following the events of the [invasion of Gilneas](/wiki/Invasion_of_Gilneas), casualties were heavy and the enemy even took the life of the prince and heir to the [Gilnean](/wiki/Gilneas_(kingdom)) throne, [Liam Greymane](/wiki/Liam_Greymane).

web.title: Invasion of Gilneas
web.description: The **invasion of Gilneas**[1] is a battle between the [Forsaken](/wiki/Forsaken) and the [worgen](/wiki/Worgen) for control of [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_peninsula). It is an important part of the [Alliance-Horde war](/wiki/Alliance-Horde_war)

The people of **Gilneas** are a [nation](/wiki/Gilneas_(kingdom)) of survivors. Having walled themselves off from the rest of humanity, they now face threats from neighboring lands as well as from within, which quickly threaten to tear their kingdom apart.

Their leader, [King Genn Greymane](/wiki/Genn_Greymane), currently resides in [Stormwind Keep](/wiki/Stormwind_Keep), within [Stormwind City](/wiki/Stormwind_City). There, he acts as one of King [Anduin Wrynn](/wiki/Anduin_Wrynn)'s primary advisers.

Others remain [human](/wiki/Human) in exile from their homeland.[1]

Knowing that her own death approached, Sylvanas could think only of her sister, Alleria, and gazed upon a necklace gifted to her by her elder sibling. Sylvanas mused that they would likely be reunited soon. Sylvanas' final stand was against Arthas himself just east of Fairbreeze Village,[26]

web.description: **Lorna Crowley** is the daughter of Lord [Darius Crowley](/wiki/Darius_Crowley), one of the principal leaders during the [Gilneas civil war](/wiki/Gilneas_civil_war). She aids [Worgen adventurers](/wiki/Worgen_(playable)) in retaking [Gilneas City](/wiki/Gilneas_City) after the first assault of the Forsaken. Later on, she obtains explosives on an [orc gunship](/wiki/Gunship) and [uses it as a ram](/wiki/Quest:Endgame) to destroy the Forsaken forward camp next to the [Greymane Wall](/wiki/Greymane_Wall).

web.title: Northgate rebels
web.description:
| Secondary leaders | [Lorna Crowley](/wiki/Lorna_Crowley) |

As a known supporter of the Alliance, [Lord Darius Crowley](/wiki/Darius_Crowley) considered his king's decisions to be "tyranny", and sent a platoon of his own soldiers, in the form of the [Gilneas Brigade](/wiki/Gilneas_Brigade_(Warcraft_III)), to aid [Lady Jaina Proudmoore](/wiki/Lady_Jaina_Proudmoore)'s expedition to [Kalimdor](/wiki/Kalimdor). When Greymane tried to reason with the nobleman, Crowley refused and insisted that he was doing what was best for the future of Gilneas. The king angrily accused Crowley of committing treason against Gilneas, while Crowley, unrepentant for his actions, started a rebellion, gathering like-minded Gilneans including his daughter [Lorna](/wiki/Lorna_Crowley) and [Tobias Mistmantle](/wiki/Tobias_Mistmantle) in forming the Northgate rebels.[1]

The day of the attack, [Lorna Crowley](/wiki/Lorna_Crowley) and a Gilnean [adventurer](/wiki/Adventurer) worked together to find Crowley's hidden arsenal,[8] and let it at the disposal of the king and his men.[9]

web.title: Darius Crowley
web.description:
| Relative(s) | [Lorna](/wiki/Lorna_Crowley) (daughter) |

When the [Burning Legion](/wiki/Burning_Legion) returned to assault Azeroth, Darius and his daughter [Lorna](/wiki/Lorna_Crowley) joined Genn on the *[Skyfire](/wiki/The_Skyfire)* as part of his army forces.

But Crowley refused, and insisted that he was doing what was best for the future of Gilneas, that he would end the King's "tyranny", and started a rebellion against Greymane, gathering like-minded Gilneans including his daughter [Lorna](/wiki/Lorna_Crowley) and [Tobias Mistmantle](/wiki/Tobias_Mistmantle) in forming the [Northgate rebellion](/wiki/Northgate_rebellion). The resulting civil war weakened the kingdom and split the populace into two groups, "royalist" and "rebel", labels that continued to spark fights years after the event ended. He was eventually arrested on the grounds of treason and held at [Stoneward Prison](/wiki/Stoneward_Prison).

With Godfrey's help the Forsaken successfully captured Darius's daughter [Lorna](/wiki/Lorna_Crowley).[8] Crowley led the Alliance's final push into [Silverpine Forest](/wiki/Silverpine_Forest). [Sylvanas Windrunner](/wiki/Sylvanas_Windrunner) herself rode out to meet with Darius at the shattered [Greymane Wall](/wiki/Greymane_Wall) and gave him two choices - the surrender of the Gilneas Liberation Front, or Lorna's death and resurrection as one of the Forsaken. Without a moment of hesitation, Darius agreed to surrender the Gilneas City in order to protect his daughter.[9] Sylvanas allowed them to retreat to Gilneas,[10] which was still contested between the Alliance and the Horde.

web.title: Margaret
web.description: **Margaret** was a [human](/wiki/Human) from [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_peninsula) and neighbor to [Lorna Crowley](/wiki/Lorna_Crowley). She gave her advice to board up her windows and buy a reinforced door to which she agreed. Lorna was also going to give her a mastiff to protect her children once they were trained. Along with the letter, Lorna gave her a bit of gun powder to protect herself as a thank you for helping her father.[1] Her current whereabouts are unknown.

**Crowley Orchard** was an apple orchard located south and very close to the town of [Duskhaven](/wiki/Duskhaven) in southwestern [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_(starting_zone)). The [farm](/wiki/Farm) was owned by the [Crowley](/wiki/Crowley) family, as the name suggests. [Lorna Crowley](/wiki/Lorna_Crowley) was here during the [invasion of Gilneas](/wiki/Invasion_of_Gilneas) until the land was swallowed by the sea.

- During the *[Catacylsm](/wiki/World_of_Warcraft:_Cataclysm)* beta, Lorna was watched over by a [Son of Goldrinn](/wiki/Son_of_Goldrinn) while staying at the orchard.

web.title: House of Greymane
web.description:
After Archibald's death, Genn took the throne and led Gilneas much like his father had. At some point, Genn met his wife, Mia, at the Royal Aderic Banquet, and theirs was not an arranged marriage. They had two children: Liam, his son and heir, and Tess, who would have died in infancy if not for the intervention of the Royal Chemist, Krennan Aranas. Genn was gruff with his children, and rarely told them he loved them.

Following the invasion of Gilneas, the Greymane family settled in Stormwind City. However, Queen Mia made sure to spend half her time in Darnassus to support her people settled at the Howling Oak, and was a frequent visitor to their encampment. When Tess wished to become a worgen, so she could better know the plight of her people to better rule them when she becomes queen, Mia redirected her to Vassandra Stormclaw in Duskwood. After her daughter left, Mia reassured Genn and explained that Tess was searching for answers to questions she never thought she would ask since the death of Liam. When her husband asked what would happen if things went wrong, she replied that they would have another one of those pleasant family conversations.
